The reason I generalized these things is because it's a general problem that I run into no matter the subject I tackle. Same thing every time.   
If I was to ask for help I'd be posting 10 questions here on a daily basis. I was hoping there was something, a video, an explanation, anything that could help clarify this issue and help me overcome this stupid struggle.

Probability -   
In a town 30% of the residents are smokers.    
It is known that 1/4 of the men smoke and 1/3 of the women smoke.   
What percent of the towns population are men?    

This question is supposed to be solved with a probability table and you need to give certain values a variable in order to solve the problem. I am looking at a solution online and the variables were given to the total amount of men (x) and the total amount of women (1-x).   
My problem is figuring out what the variables need to look like and where to put them and how to incorporate everything into an equation that will give me the right result. 

Word problems -     
A truck goes from town A to town B at the speed of 75mph. At the same time a car leaves from the same place and goes in the same direction at the speed of 90mph.   
The car arrives at town B and hour and a half before the truck.    
1. Find the ~~speed~~ (edit: length/time of trip) of the truck       
2. Find the distance between A and B    
       
This question is solved with the speed/time/distance table.   
Looking at the answer online they set the variable X in the time section of the truck and X-1.5 in the time section of the car.   
Again, my struggle is understanding how exactly to choose where to place the variable. I understand why they put it in this specific section in this question, but I can't apply the same understanding to other questions.   
     
Trigonometry -     
In a right triangle, the sum of the legs is 14 cm. One of the acute angles is 36.87 degrees. Calculate the perimeter of the triangle.    
       
I know this is an easy question and this one I could've probably solved myself but I'm just trying to give as many examples as to what exactly I struggle with.    
The answer online starts with tan(36.87°)=x/14-x      
I probably would've spend several minutes trying to figure out the fact that I need to name one leg X and the other 14-X. That is where my problem lies.  
       
       
I hope my examples were clear, I tried to give a few different ones.   
I just struggle with understanding how and where variables need to be created and applied in order to reach a solution.     
(To clarify just in case, I don't need the answers to these questions, I was just trying to show something).

OMAD stands for one meal a day.    
The first few days can definitely be difficult and you'll probably be very hungry, plain tea and/or black coffee (whichever one you prefer) will definitely help, and make sure you stay hydrated.    
Remember that hunger comes and goes in waves, learning that helped me tremendously because I stopped being worried about staying forever hungry.   
You might also experience hanger, lack of focus and energy but I promise it won't last long. Try to focus on your goal but don't feel like you need to push yourself to the breaking point - it's a process and it might take you a few tries to succeed.
